doc.title: Dave Liebman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The last discography entry and being the last three-records-a-year musician
summary: Kirchner reaches 2010; Liebman jokes that he is the last dinosaur recording three records a year and says self-production lacks a label's help.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: And that, ladies and gentlemen, is all I got.
So what – I’m just curious. The last entry is?
With Abercrombie. Marc and Abercrombie, yeah?
With Marc, Abercrombie, Drew Gress, Billy Hart.
Okay. They’re pretty recent. I just have about five since then, but that’s good.
I’ve been very – there’s been a lot going on. There’s more coming out this year.
I am the last dinosaur. The bones will be extinct, and I’m going to be on the top layer as the last generation that lasted to walk the earth.
The last guy to record three records a year. I still . . .

Self-production is great. I know it’s the only game in town for the young guys. I understand that. But, I’m sorry, unless you’re on it 20 hours a day, it’s still better to have some guy doing it for you, at least from our standpoint.
